1. On July 4, 2022, Meta Platforms, Inc. invoked its Child Sexual Exploitation
policy against my Facebook account and cut off the contracts I performed through it. I sued

them in September 2025. Meta filed a motion to dismiss. Meta did not staple a CyberTipline

report to the motion.

2. When Meta’s co-defendants’ lawyers asserted that a “legitimate violation by

Ballentine is consistent with the facts” while repeatedly putting my name beside the words

“child sexual exploitation” in their papers, I sued them in February 2026. Defendants filed

motions to dismiss. Defendants did not staple a CyberTipline report to their motions.

3. I_sent_ Advanced Notice of Intended Subpoenas to NCMEC in April
concerning those two cases, and their attorney, Ms. Hall, sent me two letters associating my

full legal name, “Marvelle J. Ballentine,” with two CyberTipline reports. I sued them in May

2026 because I have never even used my full legal name to operate any social media account.

& Exploited Children (NCMEC’) provides its written responses as detailed below. NCMEC

Ballentine, and/or (3) the account-level identifier jaychizza@icloud.com between July 1, 2022

and the present.”

7. So, that leaves the remaining questions up for determination: Where did my

legal name come from? How and why did it arrive on those letters? Did either of the two

asserted CyberTipline reports, as originally received by NCMEC, actually identify
“Marvelle J. Ballentine’? Did Meta submit either report? Why did NCMEC and Hall act
before formal service? Why did they not wait the five days until April 27, when one court

temporarily stayed discovery, or the nine days until May 1, when discovery in the other

action was temporarily stayed? Where did the urgency come from?

8. I bring six counts: conspiracy under 42 U.S.C. § 1985(2) and Virginia law

against all Defendants, for letters sent to frighten me out of my own lawsuits; defamation,

intentional infliction of emotional distress, and insulting words against Hall and NCMEC,
for what the letters said and to whom. This Complaint adds NCMEC’s Chief Legal Officer,

Panayiota Souras, who, on information and belief, approved the wording of the letters and

authorized Hall to send them before formal service. The defamation and insulting-words

counts are also asserted against Souras; Count III remains against Hall and NCMEC.
